body.statement: Let \(\widetilde C_n\) be any replacement \((\epsilon_n,\delta_n)\)-differentially private interval with \(\inf_{Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}}\Pr_Q\{\tau_Q^{\mathrm c}(x_0)\in\widetilde C_n\}\ge1-\eta\). If \(\delta_n\le c_0/n\), then \(\sup_{Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}}\mathbb E_Q[\operatorname{length}(\widetilde C_n)]\ge c\{n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}\vee(n\epsilon_n)^{-\gamma/(\gamma+d)}\}\). The lower bound uses only a randomized-treatment, uniform-design, positive-density regression submodel and contains no \(q<\gamma\) paired-cell branch.
body.justification: This theorem separates the sound full-class privacy limitation from the stronger attainable-submodel upper result.
body.gap: Existing private pointwise regression bounds concern noncausal regression experiments; the theorem embeds that barrier into honest causal intervals on the unchanged positive-density class.
body.consumer: Reviewers and privacy-budget committees obtain a defensible lower benchmark without relying on the rejected paired-microcell transport argument.
